run.question: My signup service is failing and users can't register. What should I check to debug this issue?

report.summary: The user-named service exists as Deployment signup-service (and its 2 pods) in namespace app-162. Its pods are Running but not Ready: /ready returns 503 because the signup app's check of http://payments-service:8080 fails with 'Connection refused' every 5 s (both signup pods, 07:36:16–07:36:31Z). The dependency payments-service (same namespace) is itself failing for a content reason stated in its own log: 'STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', and its /health and /ready return 503 with 'Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key'. Because the payments-service pod never becomes ready, the payments-service Endpoints object holds the pod only under notReadyAddresses, which is consistent with signup's connection refused. So signup registration failure traces to a dependency: payments-service, whose container environment takes STRIPE_API_KEY from a Secret I cannot read. Both workloads, their ReplicaSets, and all three pods were created at 2026-11-21T07:36:10Z (revision 1, image python:3.11-slim), i.e. the pods are ~20 s old at observation time; they have 0 restarts and no crash/OOM/Eviction evidence, so this is a deterministic configuration failure, not a crash loop. Prometheus and Jaeger were unavailable in this Run, so there are no metrics or traces, no error-rate or latency baseline, and no evidence on when the bad key was introduced (change_history is not integrated).

claims.text: Deployment app-162/signup-service has spec.replicas=2 and status unavailableReplicas=2 with condition Available=False (reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable, message 'Deployment does not have minimum availability.'); its container env sets PAYMENTS_SERVICE_URL=http://payments-service:8080 and takes DATABASE_URL from a Secret reference (value redacted).

Deployment app-162/payments-service has 1 replica and status unavailableReplicas=1 with condition Available=False (reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable); its container env takes STRIPE_API_KEY and DATABASE_URL from Secret references (values redacted) and its readiness probe is HTTP GET /ready:8080, liveness HTTP GET /health:8080.

Pods signup-service-7c89545dc9-jghhk and signup-service-7c89545dc9-wm9lz are phase Running with ready=false and restartCount=0, condition Ready=False/ContainersNotReady ('containers with unready status: [signup-service]'); pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-x7zwx is also Running, ready=false, restartCount=0 with the same ContainersNotReady condition. All three were created 2026-11-21T07:36:10Z and owned by their ReplicaSets.

payments-service container log states '2026-11-21 07:36:12,932 - ERROR - STRIPE_API_KEY is set to invalid test key - service will fail', and repeats '07:36:20,914 - ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key' and '07:36:30,914 - ERROR - Health check failed: Invalid Stripe API key', with GET /health and GET /ready returning 503 at 07:36:16–07:36:31Z.

Both signup-service pods log 'Payments service check failed: <urlopen error [Errno 111] Connection refused>' every ~5 s (07:36:16, 07:36:21, 07:36:26, 07:36:31) followed by 'GET /ready HTTP/1.1" 503'; these are the only in-window log lines of those pods apart from the startup line, and no database error appears in them.

The Endpoints object for payments-service lists only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.114 (pod payments-service-6d94c44fdc-x7zwx) on port 8080, and the Endpoints object for signup-service lists only notReadyAddresses 10.244.0.112 and 10.244.0.113 (the two signup pods); neither Service has a ready backend address.

Service payments-service is ClusterIP 10.96.91.175 port 8080 with selector app=payments-service and Service signup-service is ClusterIP 10.96.225.56 port 8080 with selector app=signup-service, so the names/selectors/ports do match the pods' labels (no selector mismatch).

The 17 events returned for namespace app-162 inside the window are only Normal reasons: Deployment/signup-service ScalingReplicaSet 'Scaled up replica set signup-service-7c89545dc9 from 0 to 2' and Deployment/payments-service 'Scaled up replica set payments-service-6d94c44fdc from 0 to 1' at 07:36:10Z, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started; no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Failed reason appears among those returned events.

Each Deployment has exactly one ReplicaSet (payments-service-6d94c44fdc revision 1 with 1 replica, signup-service-7c89545dc9 revision 1 with 2 replicas), both created 2026-11-21T07:36:10Z with image python:3.11-slim and owned by their Deployment; there is no older/previous ReplicaSet for either workload.

ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config defines fault-injection flags 'paymentFailure' (Fail payment service charge requests n%) and 'paymentUnreachable' (Payment service is unavailable) with defaultVariant 'off' (state ENABLED); the same file also defines cartFailure, adFailure and others, all defaultVariant 'off'.

Of the 26 deployments returned cluster-wide, all 24 otel-demo deployments (including ad, cart, checkout, currency, email, frontend, frontend-proxy, image-provider, payment, product-catalog, quote, recommendation, shipping) report readyReplicas and availableReplicas 1, and their pods report ready=true; only app-162/signup-service and app-162/payments-service show no ready replicas. This is object status only and does not by itself prove those services are error-free.

Payments-service is listening (it answers the kubelet's /ready and /health probes on 8080 with 503), so signup's 'Connection refused' is most consistently explained by the payments-service having no ready endpoint (Service with only notReadyAddresses), not by a missing listener or a Service/selector misconfiguration; the evidence for this is the 503 probe responses from the payments pod plus the notReady-only Endpoints object, but a direct in-cluster connection attempt could not be made (no exec tool).

The invalid Stripe key is supplied through the Secret referenced by payments-service's STRIPE_API_KEY env entry; the Secret's name and value are redacted and Secrets cannot be read in this Run, so the exact Secret object holding the bad key and the moment it was set are not verified.

The otel-demo flagd fault-injection flags 'paymentUnreachable'/'paymentFailure' were considered as a cause of the app-162 failure and are not supported: both are at defaultVariant 'off' in flagd-config, and they belong to the otel-demo demo app while the failing services are app-162/signup-service and app-162/payments-service (plain python:3.11-slim images) whose own logs name an invalid Stripe API key instead.

A crash/restart or resource-pressure cause for the app-162 workloads was considered and is not supported by what was returned: all three pods have restartCount=0, no previous container instance exists, and the returned app-162 events contain no OOMKilled, Evicted, BackOff or Failed reason; a readiness-probe 'Unhealthy' event that appeared once in the cluster-wide grouping could not be inspected in detail (it was not in the namespace-level event list).

Replace the invalid Stripe API key in the Secret used by Deployment payments-service STRIPE_API_KEY (verify the value out-of-band, since Secrets are unreadable here), roll payments-service, and confirm /health and /ready return 200 and that payments-service Endpoints gains a ready address; then confirm each signup-service pod's /ready returns 200 and that signup-service Endpoints has ready addresses.

Also validate the other Secret-sourced setting, DATABASE_URL, for both app-162 workloads when the key is fixed, and add an alert on payments-service readiness/health and on signup-service ready-endpoint count so a dependency-credential failure pages before users cannot register.

gaps: Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable in this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query, get_metric_names, get_label_values and traces_list_services all returned status=error / SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE. Therefore no error-rate, latency, availability time series, no kube-state-metrics history and no trace chains exist for app-162/signup-service or app-162/payments-service; ERROR-metric values are unknown, not zero, and no latency trend can be stated.

Secret values are unreadable and the Secret names in the Deployment env are redacted ('[REDACTED_CREDENTIAL]'), so the STRIPE_API_KEY value and the Secret holding it could not be verified; the conclusion that payments-service runs with an invalid test key rests on the container's own error log line, not on comparing the key value.

change_history is not an integrated data source in this Run, so when or by whom the invalid key / new Deployment revision was introduced is unknown. The workloads, ReplicaSets and pods all carry creation time 2026-11-21T07:36:10Z and revision 1, and objects are only observed as of the query time; what existed in app-162 before that time is unknown, and I cannot say whether this is a first deployment or a replacement.

No exec tool is available, so runbook steps that require kubectl exec (curl to http://payments-service:8080/health from a signup pod, and reading STRIPE_*/DATABASE_* from the container environment) could not be carried out; the Service/Endpoints objects were used instead.

Queries for networkpolicies and resourcequotas returned zero objects (status=no_data): an empty result only shows those queries matched nothing, so NetworkPolicy/ResourceQuota causes of 'Connection refused' remain unchecked/unknown rather than excluded.

Two event reads dropped events outside the authorized window (3 and 5 events), and the 'Unhealthy' Pod reason counted once for namespace app-162 in the cluster-wide grouping was not present in the namespace-level event list, so its detail (which pod, which probe, exact time) is unknown.

The similarly named but different entity otel-demo/payment (pod payment-6f7bc865d6-9z92d) was spot-checked: a log filter err|error|fail|stripe|exception|panic over the window returned no matching lines (status=no_data), which is only that the query matched nothing, not proof that service is healthy; a pod-list query with label_selector app=payment in otel-demo returned no objects, so its labels differ from the app label used in app-162.
next_steps: Out-of-band, verify the intended Stripe key and the Secret object referenced by Deployment payments-service (namespace app-162) env STRIPE_API_KEY, then update it and roll the deployment.

After the key is corrected, confirm payments-service /ready and /health return 200, that Endpoints payments-service shows a ready address, and that both signup-service pods report /ready 200 and become ready (kubectl get pods -n app-162).
Verify DATABASE_URL for both workloads resolves to a reachable database once payments-service is healthy, since registration depends on it and its value could not be read.
Run the same health checks from inside a signup pod (curl http://payments-service:8080/health) once an exec-capable tool is available, to confirm the refused-connection path directly.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger availability for this target so error-rate, latency and trace evidence can corroborate the current log/status-only conclusion.

data.alerting_rules.yml:
groups:
- name: opspilot-lab
  rules:
  - alert: CheckoutPlaceOrderErrorRatioHigh
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of checkout PlaceOrder server
        spans ended in error over the last 5 minutes.'
      summary: checkout PlaceOrder error ratio above 50%
    expr: |
      label_replace(label_replace(
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[5m])))
        /
        (sum by (k8s_namespace_name, service_name) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{k8s_namespace_name="otel-demo",service_name="checkout",span_kind="SPAN_KIND_SERVER",span_name=~".*CheckoutService/PlaceOrder"}[5m])))
      , "namespace", "$1", "k8s_namespace_name", "(.*)"), "service", "$1", "service_name", "(.*)")
      > 0.5
    for: 2m
    labels:
      cluster: opspilot-m1
      opspilot_integration_id: m0-otel-20260909
      severity: critical
- name: opspilot-self
  rules:
  - alert: OpsPilotAgentAbsent
    annotations:
      description: role {{ $labels.role }} ({{ $labels.instance }}) has not answered
        /metrics for 2 minutes.
      summary: an OpsPilot health listener is down or the worker is not scraped
    expr: up{job="opspilot"} == 0 or absent(up{job="opspilot",role="worker"})
    for: 2m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
  - alert: OpsPilotModelCallsFailing
    annotations:
      description: '{{ $value }} consecutive model calls failed on {{ $labels.instance
        }}.'
      summary: OpsPilot model calls are failing
    expr: opspilot_model_consecutive_failures >= 2
    for: 1m
    labels:
      opspilot_self: "true"
      severity: critical
